did_you_know.text: Did you know? Jotham became king at the age of twenty-five and reigned in Jerusalem for sixteen years. His mother was Jerushah, the daughter of Zadok.

Did you know? Jotham did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his father Uzziah had done. Unlike his father, however, he did not enter the temple of the LORD. Nevertheless, the people continued in their corrupt ways.
Did you know? One of Jotham’s building projects was the construction of the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, as well as extensive building on the wall of Ophel.
Did you know? Jotham built cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the wooded regions he built fortresses and towers for defense and protection.

Did you know? After Jotham defeated the Ammonites, they gave him one hundred talents of silver and twenty thousand kors of grain that same year—ten thousand kors of wheat and ten thousand kors of barley.
Did you know? The Ammonites continued to make these payments to Jotham in the second and third years as well, so the payments lasted for three years.
Did you know? The Bible attributes Jotham’s growing strength to the fact that he prepared and ordered his ways before the LORD his God.
Did you know? Jotham’s deeds, wars, and ways were recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah, which served as a documented source for the account of his reign.
Did you know? The Bible again records Jotham’s age when he began to reign and the length of his reign: he was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem for sixteen years.
Did you know? After Jotham died, he was buried in the City of David, and his son Ahaz succeeded him as king.
